tool_input.description: Fix GOPATH multi-entry and FakeSpawner map copy
tool_input.prompt:
Two Copilot findings on PR #261, branch `feat/daemon-test-harness` in <repo>. I verified both — both valid. Commit, do not push.

**1. `Makefile:96` — `GOPATH` can be a colon-separated list, and the fallback breaks on it.**

```make
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOBIN)
ifeq ($(GOINSTALL_BIN),)
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOPATH)/bin
endif
```

I reproduced it:

```
$ GOPATH=/tmp/a:/tmp/b go env GOPATH        → /tmp/a:/tmp/b
  naive suffix gives                        → /tmp/a:/tmp/b/bin
  as a PATH prefix that contributes         → /tmp/a  and  /tmp/b/bin
  go install actually writes to             → /tmp/a/bin     (first entry)
```

So on a multi-entry `GOPATH`, `PATH` gains two wrong directories and not the real one, `exec.LookPath("ethos")` fails, and we are back in precisely the loop this fix was meant to close: provisioning succeeds, tests fail "ethos not found on PATH", and the remedy message names the command the developer just ran.

Take the first colon-separated entry for the fallback. Keep `GOBIN` taking precedence — when `GOBIN` is set, `go install` honors it regardless of `GOPATH`, and `GOBIN` is a single directory by definition.

Worth naming why this keeps happening: this is the **third** instance in this PR of a defect invisible from my machine — after `IsolateEthos` symlinking my global archetypes tree, and `make test` not putting the install dir on `PATH` at all. My `GOPATH` is single-entry, so I cannot reproduce this locally without forcing it. When you fix it, add a brief comment explaining the multi-entry case so the next person doesn't "simplify" it back.

**2. `internal/daemontest/daemontest.go:99` — `FakeSpawner` records `envOverrides` by reference.**

The map is stored as passed. If a caller mutates it after `Run` returns, or reuses one map across concurrent calls, recorded call data silently changes, and under `-race` concurrent read/write of that map is a genuine race.

Nothing in the tier does this today, so it is latent — but a test fixture whose recorded evidence can change after the fact is the wrong shape, particularly in a harness whose entire purpose is trustworthy assertions. Copy the map on record so each call captures an immutable snapshot. Handle nil correctly (a nil map should stay distinguishable from an empty one if any assertion depends on that — check whether any does before deciding).

Consider whether anything else `FakeSpawner` records has the same aliasing problem, and say so either way.

**Tests:** for (2), a test that mutates the passed map after `Run` and asserts the recorded copy is unchanged — verify it fails against the current code first. For (1), a Makefile change is not unit-testable, so verify by forcing a multi-entry `GOPATH` and confirming the computed `GOINSTALL_BIN` is the first entry's `bin` — show the command and output.

`make check`, commit, do not push. Report both fixes, the multi-entry verification output, and your finding on other aliasing in `FakeSpawner`.

# go install places a binary in $GOBIN if set, else $GOPATH/bin -- neither is
# guaranteed to already be on PATH. Without this, `make test` provisions
# ethos successfully but exec.LookPath("ethos") still fails: tools-ethos
# ran, the binary exists, and the remedy message points right back at the
# command that was just run. Computed once, at parse time, so every `test`
# invocation prepends the same directory `go install` actually used.
#
# GOPATH may be a colon-separated list (":"-joined on every GOOS, including
# darwin and linux -- Go never uses the OS path-list separator here). `go
# install` with no GOBIN always writes to the FIRST entry's bin/, so take
# only that entry -- appending /bin to the whole list would name a directory
# nothing was ever installed to, and would also inject a second, wrong
# directory onto PATH.
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOBIN)
ifeq ($(GOINSTALL_BIN),)
GOINSTALL_BIN := $(shell go env GOPATH | cut -d: -f1)/bin
endif
